positions.claim: Even granting full model capability, human recall is materially faster than querying an agent, so students should keep learning things themselves rather than outsourcing cognition.
Companies at the frontier — Stripe and the labs alike — still pay an enormous premium for raw cognitive ability, which is revealed-preference evidence against renouncing learning.
LLMs have not yet produced a genuinely compelling essay, likely because the reward signal for good writing is hard to define for RL.
Dropping out of college carries essentially zero long-term reputational cost, and is reversible — he did it twice and returned in between.
His youthful belief that startup opportunities were fleeting was wrong; Silicon Valley has reliably had a surfeit of opportunities over many decades.
The current moment is not the last window to start a company — he'd take the under on that claim, comparing the panic to millenarian reactions like post-aviation utopianism.
Grounding in a concrete, viscerally felt customer problem is what makes a hard, unglamorous idea survivable; imagined customer problems are the failure mode.

A long pre-launch period is acceptable only if you have a continuous stream of real production users; Stripe waited two years to launch but had a paying customer two months in and added customers every month.
In most domains other than heavily regulated infrastructure, waiting two years to launch is the wrong call.
The classic lean-startup path of finding a small niche via ads and expanding is becoming more competitive and crowded, so founders should aggressively decorrelate instead.
Many of the most successful companies of the last decade — the labs, Anduril — are explicitly anti-lean-startup in how they began.
Lean startup dominated 20 years ago because of capital constraints and the absence of AI; AI now makes standing up a broad-capability organization cheap enough to start ambitious up front.
Founders should evaluate the success case, not just the failure case, before raising significant money — whether they want to do this work for 10, 17, or 30 years.
Fear that the big labs will expand into and crush startup ideas is overstated, because large organizations cannot successfully prosecute 100 priorities at once — as Google's checkered record shows.
Improving model capabilities will genuinely obviate some specific verticals and tasks, and already has in certain domains — a distinct risk from the labs competing directly.
New businesses started on Stripe are up around 2x year-over-year, the largest relative jump Stripe has recorded, versus roughly 50% during the 2020 COVID inflection.

The surge in new businesses is not just low-quality vibe-coded output: the median business is performing better than a year ago, probability of hitting revenue thresholds is rising, and Atlas time-to-revenue is declining.
Startup growth is accelerating primarily because incumbents now perceive the risk of the status quo as higher than the risk of adopting unproven vendors.
AI will not centralize the economy into a small number of winners; the trend lines point to many thousands of winners and more broad-based prosperity.
A business with many operational schleps can still be intellectually rich, because each customer is an applied theory about how some part of the world works.
